docs.title: Repair issues
docs.text: Four checks surface as Home Assistant repair issues (Settings → System → Repairs) rather than only a log line, because a log line only reaches someone tailing it at the right moment. None of the four stop the integration from running — each one means something is quietly not being decided the way you probably expect, until you act on it. None are auto-fixable from the Repairs UI (is_fixable: false); every fix below is made in the configuration itself.

docs.title: Fixture drift
docs.text:
Cause. You have set a Fixture to compare against (Configure → Execution → fixture_path) — typically a YAML file kept in a checkout alongside the integration, used as a second source of truth for your configuration — and the live subentries no longer match what that file describes. Evaluated on every setup of this entry — at Home Assistant startup, and again on every reload after that (for example after an edit).

Effect. Nothing about the running decision changes. This only means the two no longer agree, so anything that trusts the fixture as "what the house actually runs" (a test suite, a migration check) is comparing against a stale picture.

Fix. Re-import the file (the import_config service) to bring the live configuration back in line with it, or re-export the live configuration to that path if the live configuration is the one you actually intend to keep. No restart needed: fixing the cause and letting the automatic reload land clears it. If you have no fixture_path configured, you will never see this issue at all — it only applies to the specific workflow of keeping a configuration file and the live subentries in sync on purpose.

docs.title: Unknown entities
docs.text:
Cause. The configuration names at least one entity id that exists in neither Home Assistant's state machine nor its entity registry — evaluated once Home Assistant has finished starting, and again on every reload of the entry after that (for example after an edit).

Effect. A rule, condition or guard that depends on a missing entity behaves as though that input were permanently absent (falling back to whatever default: it states, or simply never matching). A blind among the named entities can never be moved at all, by anything.

Fix. Either create the missing helper/entity, or edit the configuration to reference the entity your house actually has. The issue's own description lists exactly which entities and how many. No restart needed: fixing the cause and letting the automatic reload land clears it.

docs.title: Blinds missing features
docs.text:
Cause. A blind's rules ask it to do something its cover.* entity does not actually support — evaluated once Home Assistant has finished starting, and again on every reload of the entry after that (for example after an edit). The entity picker for "which cover is this blind" filters only on the cover domain, so it is possible to pick a garage door or an awning that has no tilt channel, or no position setter at all.

Effect. Nothing crashes — the command the hardware cannot carry out is simply dropped silently at the point it would be sent, which otherwise looks exactly like a dead-band skip or a withheld guard with no obvious cause.

Fix. Either pick a cover entity that genuinely supports what the rules ask for, or narrow the rules to only what the entity can do: position: 0 and position: 100 need only open/close support, anything strictly between needs a position setter, and tilt needs a tilt channel at all. No restart needed: fixing the cause and letting the automatic reload land clears it.

docs.title: Configuration has warnings
docs.text:
Cause. validate() found one or more warning-severity problems in the configuration — evaluated once Home Assistant has finished starting, and again on every reload of the entry after that (for example after an edit), exactly like the two issues above. Possible causes (not an exhaustive list, but the common ones): a zone with no rules at all, a rule that can never be reached because an earlier one in the same list already matches everything, a guard that can never fire, a blind no zone claims, a tilt value asked of a blind with no tilt axis, or a computed slat_angle asked of a blind that states no facade or slat geometry, or placed on the wrong axis.

Effect. Nothing stops working outright — every one of these means some specific thing is quietly not being decided, the same class of fault as the two issues above, just caught by the broader structural checker rather than by looking at live entities.

Fix. The issue's own description lists every warning found, by code and message, naming the affected subentry. Open that subentry (zone, rule, guard, or blind) from the options menu and either fix what it names, or — if the behaviour really is what you intended — nothing further is required; the issue exists so you confirm that on purpose, not so it fixes itself. No restart needed: fixing the cause and letting the automatic reload land clears it.

docs.title: sensor.cover_logic_mode
docs.text:
The one diagnostic entity this integration creates. Its state is the currently active mode (home, night, whatever your configuration names); its attributes are the full decision behind that mode and how the executor acted on it. It is unavailable only before the first evaluation has ever completed — after that, a later failing evaluation keeps showing the last good decision rather than going blank, with the failure surfaced through last_error instead.

readiness and pending are both nested objects, not flat attributes — if you are searching the entity's attributes for a blind's name or an entity id, search inside readiness.blocked and pending.deferred/ pending.queued as well as at the top level, or you will miss it.

docs.title: targets
docs.text: A mapping of every blind's entity id to the action decided for it this evaluation: {"position": <0-100 or "keep">, "tilt": <0-100 or "keep">}. This is the engine's answer, independent of whether the executor was actually allowed to act on it — it is populated the same way whether dry_run is on or off, and regardless of what readiness says.

docs.title: trace
docs.text: A mapping of every blind's entity id to the label of the rule that decided it — for example night.terrace#0 (zone terrace's own first rule in mode night), home.*#1 (mode home's shared default list, second rule — see rules: inherited defaults), or home.terrace#none (no rule matched at all, which decides the same thing as keep/keep). This is the first thing to read when a blind did something you did not expect — see troubleshooting.

docs.title: last_error
docs.text: The most recent evaluation failure, or None if the last evaluation succeeded. The sensor keeps showing the previous good targets/trace while this is set — a failing evaluation never blanks the entity.

docs.title: last_success
docs.text: An ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the last evaluation that completed without error, or None if none ever has.

docs.title: dry_run
docs.text: Whether the executor is only logging commands (true) or actually issuing them (false). Read live from the config entry's options, so it changes the instant you flip it on the Execution screen — no reload needed. See shadow mode.

docs.title: pending
docs.text: What is currently waiting, as two independent sub-mappings — a blind can appear in both at once, since a guard's deferral and an in-flight movement sequence are unrelated facts about it.

docs.title: pending.deferred
docs.text:
Entity id → one guard's live wait:

Field Meaning guard Which guard (by position in the guards list) is holding this. name That guard's name. policy Always defer — only a defer guard produces an entry here. stage The guard's stage (output or input). state "waiting" while the deadline has not been reached, or the resolved timeout answer (proceed/abandon) once it has. waited Seconds elapsed since the wait began. max_wait The guard's configured max_wait in seconds, or null for "wait indefinitely". on_timeout The guard's configured proceed/abandon. recheck_every How often (seconds) this wait is re-examined even with no new state change.

A deferral's clock resets to zero across a Home Assistant restart — see guards: max_wait, on_timeout, recheck_every for why that is the safe direction rather than a bug.

docs.title: pending.queued
docs.text:
Entity id → what the executor's runner is doing with it right now, listed only once a sequence actually has a command queued (an empty sequence is never listed):

Field Meaning running "<priority>/<source>" of the sequence currently executing, if any. seq That sequence's own id. step "<current>/<total>" position within the sequence (for example a position move followed by a tilt move). age How long the running sequence has been executing. waiting "<priority>/<source>" of a second request queued behind the running one, if any. waiting_age How long that second request has been queued.

This is the one thing a log line cannot show you: what has not happened yet, not what already has.

docs.title: manual_holds
docs.text: A sorted list of blind entity ids currently held because manual_detection.hold recognised a person moving them by hand. A held blind is left alone — its current target is not re-sent — until the decided target actually changes. See troubleshooting for what to check when a blind in this list seems "stuck".

docs.title: last_command
docs.text:
The single newest thing the executor did, or deliberately did not do. One of five kinds (kind field), each with its own extra fields:

kind Meaning would_call Dry run: the runner reached a command and did not send it. called Live: the runner reached a command and issued it. suppressed An axis was given a target but produced no command anyway — most often the dead band, or an axis the blind does not have. withheld A guard removed the whole action before the runner ever saw it (reason, policy, guard fields explain which). dispatched The command reached hass.services.async_call and returned without raising — written after the call, so this is "accepted", where called only meant "attempted".

Every entry also carries at (an ISO-8601 UTC timestamp) and, where relevant, blind, service, and the command's own payload fields.

docs.title: readiness
docs.text:
Whether the inputs this decision depends on could actually be read, and which blinds a missing one is currently blocking. None only before the first evaluation has ever completed.

Field Meaning ready true if every entity the whole configuration reads is currently readable. missing Entity ids that are absent, unknown or unavailable and were read by some node with no stated default: — truncated to a bounded number, with missing_count giving the real total. missing_count The real count behind missing, in case the list itself was truncated. blocked Entity id (a blind) → the subset of missing that that blind's own decision reads — this is the per-blind veto; a blind absent from blocked was not stopped by this, however broken the rest of the house's inputs are.

This is the answer to "it decided something sensible-looking and moved nothing" — without it, that looks like a bug in the executor rather than a deliberate refusal to act on an incomplete picture of the world. See troubleshooting.

docs.title: matica_mode and matica_diff
docs.text:
A live comparison against a separate, external entity named sensor.zaluzie_cielovy_stav — the Jinja-template matrix this project was originally built to replace on its author's own house. This is specific to that one migration and almost certainly does not exist on your installation.

  • matica_mode — that entity's own state (its "mode"), or null if the entity does not exist.
  • matica_diff — null means "nothing to compare against" (the entity is absent, or its comparison attribute is missing or unparsable); [] means "compared, and they agree"; a non-empty list names the entities the two disagreed about. null and [] are never interchangeable — one means "not checked", the other means "checked, no disagreement found".

If you are not migrating from that specific system, treat both as always null/inert.

docs.title: Services
docs.text: Two services, the bridge between the YAML configuration format and the subentries the UI edits. Both are also reachable from Settings → Devices & services → Cover Logic → Configure → Import / export configuration, which calls the same code.

docs.title: cover_logic.import_config
docs.text:
Reads a YAML file and replaces this integration's whole configuration with it.

Field Required Default Meaning path yes — Path to the YAML file, e.g. /config/cover_logic.yaml. dry_run no false Validate and report what would change, without writing anything. overwrite no false Required to be true if the entry already has any configuration — see below.

Returns a summary (visible in Developer Tools → Actions, "Response data"): the counts of blinds, zones, modes, conditions, values and rules the file contains, how many existing subentries would be/were replaced, and any validate() warnings.

Replace, never merge. If the entry already has subentries configured and overwrite is not true, the call is refused outright — every import either replaces the whole configuration or changes nothing, so a result can never be a mix of the file you just imported and whatever was there before.

Validated before anything is written, including under dry_run: the file is parsed, checked for structural problems, and run through validate() — so a dry run reports exactly the refusal a real run would hit, never a false "this would succeed" followed by a real failure.

# Developer Tools → Actions
action: cover_logic.import_config
data:
  path: /config/cover_logic.yaml
  dry_run: true
  overwrite: true

Or have a model write the file for you. The YAML dialect is documented for exactly this: point an LLM at MODELS.md §4 and a worked example, docs/example-config.yaml, describe your house in plain language, and import the result with dry_run: true first, as above.

docs.title: cover_logic.export_config
docs.text:
Writes the current configuration — whatever the subentries hold right now, however they were built — out to a YAML file.

Field Required Default Meaning path yes — Path to write to, e.g. /config/cover_logic_export.yaml.

Refuses to write through a symlink — if path is a symlink, the export is refused rather than silently rewriting whatever the link points at. Writing directly to a real, non-symlink path is always allowed, including overwriting a file that already holds a configuration you are about to replace.

Refuses to overwrite a file that has comments. export_config writes from the parsed configuration, which carries no comments of its own — if the target file already exists and contains at least one whole-line comment, the export is refused rather than silently discarding them. Move the existing file aside, or export to a different path, and merge any comments back by hand.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Every service call that fails raises with one of these keys. The message shown always includes the specific detail ({error_detail}, {path}, {count}) for that failure.

Key Meaning no_config_entry Cover Logic is not set up yet — add the integration first. invalid_config The file parsed, but validate() found at least one error-severity problem in it. cannot_parse_file The file is not valid YAML, or not valid in this configuration's dialect. cannot_read_file The path could not be opened at all (does not exist, no permission). existing_config import_config was called without overwrite: true while subentries already exist. import_conversion_failed The file passed validate(), but converting it into subentries failed internally — this is a bug in the integration, not in your file; please report it. export_path_is_symlink export_config's path is a symlink; point it at the real file instead. export_path_is_directory path names a directory, not a file. export_parent_missing The directory path would be written into does not exist. export_target_has_comments path already exists and has comment lines that would be silently lost by exporting. nothing_to_export Nothing is configured yet, so there is nothing for export_config to write. cannot_parse_subentries The entry's current subentries could not be read back into a Config — an internal inconsistency; please report it. cannot_write_file The file could not be written (permissions, disk full, and similar).
